label: Antenna / Communications
description: Sends data down to ground stations and receives commands from mission control. On a CubeSat, this is often just a few thin metal tape measures that spring open once in orbit.

label: Solar Panels
description: Body-mounted solar cells cover the CubeSat's outer faces, converting sunlight into the only power the satellite will ever get. There's no way to refuel or recharge from the ground.

label: Onboard Computer
description: A small computer, often barely more powerful than a smartphone chip, that runs the flight software, talks to every other subsystem, and decides what the satellite does next.

label: ADCS
description: Short for Attitude Determination and Control System — the sensors and small reaction wheels or magnetorquers that keep the satellite pointed the right way, whether that's at Earth, the Sun, or a ground station.

label: Payload / Sensor
description: Whatever the mission actually needs: a camera, a radio experiment, a materials sample, or a purpose-built science instrument. Everything else on the satellite exists to support this one part.

label: Battery
description: Stores power collected by the solar panels for use during eclipse, the part of every orbit spent in Earth's shadow with no sunlight at all.

label: Structure / Frame
description: The frame holds every other subsystem in exact alignment and has to survive launch vibration, then fit precisely inside a P-POD deployer with almost no wasted space.
